why: Records-only close-out after PR #11615 MERGED (squash 2ee21f4e5, 2026-09-10T00:42:51Z, head f606e4d4d, all 6 checks green). Three record edits, no code: (1) WO-20260909-DECISION-THE-ROLLBACK-REGISTRY-IS-AN-OUTAGE lifecycle in_flight -> done with closed_at and the merge recorded in its build block — it was still reading `in_flight` on main after the merge, which is stale AND was holding one of the 8 WIP slots against another lane; (2) the OPEN-ITEMS monitoring row's `observation` said 'PR #11615 is open, Tier-2, held for a human merge click', which is now FALSE — it records the merge instead; (3) the R13 merge-slot claim this arming needs. ⚠️ NEITHER RECORD IS ALLOWED TO CLAIM MORE THAN HAPPENED, and that is the point of the edit rather than an aside: `verified_at` STAYS NULL, `clears_when` is UNTOUCHED, and both files now say in terms that a MERGE IS NOT A DEPLOY AND A DEPLOY IS NOT A TICK UNDER THE FLAG. Nobody has run the rollback, before or after the change, so the repaired rollback is exactly as unexercised as the broken one was — the row stays open and `loud`. The work object's `done` is likewise scoped in its own review_trigger to mean THE DECISION AND ITS BUILD ARE COMPLETE, explicitly not that the effect was observed on the fleet. Tier-1 by path: docs/claude/** only. No src/, no config/, no tests, no workflows; no order placed, modified or cancelled; no env var changed. ⚠️ THIS IS THE SECOND SLUG THIS CLOSE-OUT HAS TAKEN, AND THE REASON IS A MEASURED WEDGE, NOT TIDINESS. The first, `claude/mi229-closeout-records`, was created together with its arming file, so `claude-pr-automerge` opened the PR (#11623) under GITHUB_TOKEN — and that branch NEVER RECEIVED A SINGLE `pull_request` WORKFLOW RUN: measured via actions_list filtered to the branch with event=pull_request, `total_count: 0` across the PR creation and THREE subsequent ordinary pushes by a real author, re-read ~14 minutes after the open and ~7 after the last push, so it is not latency. Only `push`-event runs fired there. ⚠️ THAT CORRECTS CLAUDE.md's DOCUMENTED REMEDY for the zero-check trap, which says to push one ordinary commit to arm CI: two such commits armed nothing here. The remedy that works is the OTHER one CLAUDE.md gives — open the PR yourself first so it carries a real `pull_request` event, then push the arming file, which `claude-pr-automerge` ADOPTS rather than re-opening. That is the order used here, and it is why the first push of this branch is expected to FAIL R6/R13 as an intermediate state. Verified on the same session's own #11615, which was opened with create_pull_request and had 4 real checks within a minute.
